To continue breathing... it feels less like living and more like a slow, shameful decay. A hollow mockery of the man I was. There is no glory in surviving this, only a lingering, pathetic rot. pool.baseline: It’s a strange sensation, watching the world move at a velocity that renders my entire life's work... irrelevant. I spent forty years untangling the nuances of late-period Hegelian dialectics, and now, with these new computational models, the very ground I stood on feels like it's dissolving. It isn't just sadness. It’s a sense of profound obsolescence. It feels as though the book has been written, the final chapter is closed, and yet the physical binding persists, needlessly occupying space on a shelf where it no longer belongs.

I can still hear them... the sounds of the vanguard breaking, the screams of men I promised to protect, all because of my single, catastrophic error. I am a ghost inhabiting a living body, and the shame is a rot that won't stop spreading.
